hypotheses.claim: A typed halt rule using both state-delta and unresolved residual pressure will reduce false convergence/false halt relative to a delta-only rule on real FRANK replay episodes.
support: synthetic proxy A: delta-only falsely converged on 100% stalled toy trajectories; delta+residual-pressure produced 0% false convergence in the constructed toy set
hypotheses.falsifier: On matched H1 frozen episodes, delta+pressure fails to reduce false halt/stagnation classification versus delta-only after controlling thresholds and budgets.
hypotheses.next_test: H1 replay classification with converging, stalled, productive-cycle and diverging episodes.

hypotheses.claim: Outcome-gated adaptive recurrence will outperform one fixed recurrence budget across heterogeneous FRANK task difficulty at matched compute or matched outcome quality.
support: 2025 recurrent-depth language-model research reports gains from scaling recurrent test-time compute
2026 overthinking research reports that additional reasoning can degrade already-correct trajectories
synthetic proxy B favored adaptive stopping under deliberately heterogeneous optimum-depth assumptions
hypotheses.falsifier: A fixed budget matches or beats adaptive routing on H1 frozen episodes across outcome quality, latency, compute, false halt and recovery after threshold tuning.
hypotheses.next_test: Matched fixed-budget vs adaptive continue/halt routing on H1.

hypotheses.claim: GWT ignition/focus carries useful predictive information for whether another expensive recurrence step has positive marginal utility.
support: mechanistic compatibility only; no FRANK causal evidence yet
hypotheses.falsifier: Ignition/focus adds no predictive or causal value beyond task difficulty, residual pressure and loop-local state on held-out H1 episodes.
hypotheses.next_test: Ablate/permute GWT routing variables under matched replay.

hypotheses.claim: At least one historical regulator family (Thalamus gain/habituation, NAcc value/persistence, novelty, urgency) provides causal control benefit for loop allocation beyond descriptive logging.
hypotheses.falsifier: Lesion causes no meaningful degradation and mechanistic rescue provides no restoration across representative H1 episodes.
hypotheses.next_test: Factorial lesion/rescue with resource shadows and negative controls.

hypotheses.claim: Bounded reopening of preserved Hyperposition alternatives can rescue stalled attractors with acceptable destabilization cost.
hypotheses.falsifier: Reopening fails to improve recovery from stalled episodes or increases divergence/oscillation enough to erase outcome gains.
hypotheses.next_test: Matched stalled episodes: reopen compatible alternative vs no reopen vs random reopen.

counterhypotheses.claim: Ordinary persistent event-driven orchestration explains the useful behavior; recurrent-model mathematics adds little.
A global stability controller damages heterogeneous useful timescales; only local/typed controllers work.
Historical neuro-inspired regulators are descriptive legacy readouts with no causal control value.
Jacobian/spectral-radius style diagnostics predict numerical stability but not cognitive usefulness; outcome-gated control is necessary.
Observed cycles are epiphenomenal timing artifacts and do not causally improve task outcomes.

reason: No live Ubuntu H1 replay, target Qwen-4B reader, or regulator lesion/rescue evidence was available in this run.
